Suzuki Jimny Sierra II with a rooftop tent, 2 guests, Oct 10–12, booked under Asuka
          Umeda. Collected at the Evertrail office in Ikehara, Okinawa City; returned to the airport.

Boat fun diving out of Sesoko. Two tanks at Minna Island or Sesoko, small groups, own boat,
          and the underwater photos come free.

Warm and still swimmable; nights near 24 °C. Showers pass quickly, but wind is the real threat on an exposed pitch. October is still typhoon season — roughly a 1-in-10 chance of one within 300 km over three days, so keep a wet-weather fallback.
Calm bay with sunsets over the city. No toilets.

All 26 drivable sites in the Evertrail directory, ordered by road time from the Evertrail
      office in Okinawa City — where we collect the car. The directory prices only two of them, so
      “none posted” means unknown, not free. Book the paid ones: Oct 10–12 is the Sports Day weekend.
One backpack each. Bedding and the BBQ set come with the rental, so this is what we carry plus what we buy on landing. Tap a row to check it off, or Edit list to change it.

Night 1 is covered, night 2 is not. The set is one dinner for two — 200 g agu pork, 200 g Okinawa beef, two sausages, four yakitori, gas and the teppan grill. Buy tomorrow's meat tomorrow; a cooler will not hold it two days at 28 °C.
This is why the dive is today. Surfacing around 13:00 today leaves about 31 hours before tomorrow's 20:25 flight — comfortably past the 24 h that two dives want. Diving on Day 3 would not be safe.
Airport return closes 17:30. The booking's 18:00 slot is the Okinawa City office, so going back there instead costs an hour plus the bus. Today is Sports Day — expect traffic on Route 58.
Email to book — they are not taking calls. Staff shortage, so the phone is off; info@divenuts.jp or LINE, and replies come the same evening or the next day. Book well ahead, not the day before.
The published coordinate lands on the expressway, so the drive time is unreliable. Scout it first.
Under a road bridge in urban Nago — no beach, no view. Not recommended.
One car only — risky on a holiday weekend with a rooftop tent.
Dead-end track, very little room, and you reverse back out.
No facilities, off-road access, riverside in typhoon season. Not recommended.
Routing uses narrow forest roads that close after storms. Allow longer via Route 70.
